label: Algiers
note: The city's centre as geocoded: the point the reports' "West of Algiers" and "North of Algiers" are measured from (assumed).

label: Algiers harbour
note: The target named by the German and Italian reports. The harbour's centre, placed by hand.

label: Maison Blanche airfield
source: Hand-placed on a modern map (today's Houari Boumediene airport)
note: No. 153 Squadron's base (its record book's Place column).

label: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA)
source: Battery C morning report: "4 mi West of Algiers"
note: Four statute miles (3.48 nm) due west of the city's centre: the report gives a distance and direction, not a grid, so this is within about a mile.

label: Where the Ju 88 turned, 12 May
source: 153 Sqn summary: "turned South about two miles West of Algiers"
note: Where the Ju 88, evading anti-aircraft fire, turned south before the Beaufighter closed; it then "blew up and fell into the sea", so the wreck is somewhere offshore, not at this point. Two statute miles assumed.

label: Ju 88 destroyed, 4 June
source: 153 Sqn summary: "a Ju.88 15 miles North of Algiers"
note: Fifteen miles north of the city, at sea; statute miles assumed (13 nm). Direction and distance only.

label: Casbah

note: The old Turkish town above the harbour. Present in 1942 by the sheet; the point is today's, not read off the sheet.
